cards.explanation: The answer is wrath. John says the angels hold the seven final plagues, “…with which the wrath of God is completed.” (Revelation 15:1) Seven plagues, and then it's finished, friends. Not one more batch sitting in the back of the oven.

The answer is True. John says the people beside the sea of glass were “…holding harps from God…” (Revelation 15:2) These are the ones who conquered the beast and its image and the number of its name, and they're standing beside something like a sea of glass mixed with fire. Harps in hand, ready to sing.

The answer is God's servant Moses. Moses was Israel's leader, and the singers sing “…the song of God’s servant Moses and of the Lamb…” (Revelation 15:3) Moses and the Israelites once sang a song to the LORD too (Exodus 15:1). Two names on one song, and John gives us both.

The reason they give is that God alone is holy. They sing, “Who will not fear You, O Lord, and glorify Your name? For You alone are holy.” (Revelation 15:4) Notice the word alone, friends. They aren't comparing Him to anybody.
The answer is False. The song says, “All nations will come and worship before You, for Your righteous acts have been revealed.” (Revelation 15:4) Not a few nations. All of them.

The answer is bowls. One of the four living creatures gave the angels “…seven golden bowls full of the wrath of God, who lives forever and ever.” (Revelation 15:7) Golden bowls, and every one of them full. Keep an eye on those bowls, bakers, because the angels get their orders in the next chapter.

The answer is False. The temple is filled with smoke from God's glory and His power, and “…no one could enter the temple until the seven plagues of the seven angels were completed.” (Revelation 15:8) Nobody walks in until the plagues are done.

The answer is those with the mark of the beast. The sores break out “…on those who had the mark of the beast and worshiped its image.” (Revelation 16:2) The text names exactly who gets them. The passage keeps being that specific, friends, so keep reading carefully.
The answer is dies. The sea turns to blood “…like that of the dead, and every living thing in the sea died.” (Revelation 16:3) This is a heavy one, friends. The text says every living thing.

The reason the angel gives is that they spilled the blood of saints and prophets. He says, “For they have spilled the blood of saints and prophets, and You have given them blood to drink, as they deserve.” (Revelation 16:6) I think this one hurts to read. But the angel of the waters states the reason right there.

The answer is True. John hears the altar reply, “Yes, Lord God Almighty, true and just are Your judgments.” (Revelation 16:7) The angel of the waters speaks first, then the altar answers. Two voices, and they agree about God's judgments.

The answer is False. John says the people “…cursed the name of God, who had authority over these plagues. Yet they did not repent and give Him glory.” (Revelation 16:9) The heat came, and repenting did not.

The answer is that they curse the God of heaven. The text says the men “…curse the God of heaven for their pains and sores. Yet they did not repent of their deeds.” (Revelation 16:11) I think this is a hard verse to read, friends.

The answer is to prepare the way for the kings of the East. The sixth angel's bowl goes on the Euphrates, “…and its water was dried up to prepare the way for the kings of the East.” (Revelation 16:12) The purpose comes in the same sentence as the drying, so no guessing needed.

The answer is battle. The spirits go out to the kings of the earth “…to assemble them for battle on the great day of God the Almighty.” (Revelation 16:14) These are demonic spirits, and they perform signs as they go. I think a sign is how you get a whole crowd of kings to show up for something.

The answer is True. Right after “Behold, I am coming like a thief.” the verse says, “Blessed is the one who remains awake and clothed, so that he will not go naked and let his shame be exposed.” (Revelation 16:15) The blessing goes to the one who stays awake and clothed. A blessing in the middle of all those bowls.

The answer is “It is done!” That's the loud voice from the throne in the temple. (Revelation 16:17) It comes when the seventh angel pours out his bowl into the air. Seven bowls, seven angels, and then those words.

The quake is the greatest since people came on the earth. John lists lightning, rumblings, thunder and “…a great earthquake the likes of which had not occurred since men were upon the earth—so mighty was the great quake.” (Revelation 16:18) Nothing like it had happened since people were on the earth.

The answer is collapse. The great city was split into three parts, “…and the cities of the nations collapsed.” (Revelation 16:19) The quake doesn't stop at one city, friends. The text says the cities of the nations, plural.

The answer is True. The verse says, “And God remembered Babylon the great and gave her the cup of the wine of the fury of His wrath.” (Revelation 16:19) God is the one who remembers her and the one who gives her the cup. Nobody else hands it over, and nobody has to hold the door for it either.

The answer is True. The verse says, “And men cursed God for the plague of hail, because it was so horrendous.” (Revelation 16:21) Hailstones of almost a hundred pounds each rain down, and men curse God for that plague. Earlier, people also cursed His name (Revelation 16:9). It's a heavy way to end the bowls.
